analysis.text:
The image is a choropleth map of Karnataka districts in India, showing the Gross District Domestic Product (GDDP) in Crore (Indian Rupees). The map uses a color gradient to represent the GDDP, with darker shades indicating higher GDDP values and lighter shades indicating lower GDDP values. The legend on the right side of the map provides a scale from 20,000 or less to 1,00,000+ Crore.

The map includes the names of all 30 districts in Karnataka, with the most populous and economically developed districts, such as Bengaluru Urban and Bengaluru Rural, shown in the darkest red, indicating the highest GDDP. Other districts are shaded in varying shades of orange and yellow, representing lower GDDP values.

The source of the data is the Department of Economics & Statistics, Government of Karnataka (2023-24). The map also includes a north indicator at the bottom left corner.
